title: China's National IC Fund Leads DeepSeek's First External Funding Round at $45 Billion Valuation — State Capital Anchors China's AI Model Champion
detail: Bloomberg, citing a Financial Times report, confirmed on May 6–7, 2026 that China's state-backed National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund (the 'Big Fund' — Guojia Jicheng Dianlu Chanye Touzi Jijin, or 国家集成电路产业投资基金) is leading negotiations for DeepSeek's first external funding round, targeting a valuation of $45 billion. TechCrunch and TechNode independently confirmed the report. The $45 billion valuation represents a dramatic acceleration from the $20 billion+ estimates from weeks earlier — when Tencent and Alibaba were initially reported as potential investors — and reflects both global recognition of DeepSeek's technical achievements (V4 natively optimized for Huawei Ascend hardware) and Beijing's strategic determination to formally designate DeepSeek as a state-sponsored national AI champion. Founded by Liang Wenfeng from the High-Flyer (幻方科技) quantitative hedge fund, DeepSeek has been entirely self-funded through its V1, V2, V3, R1, and V4 model generations — making this the first external capital raise in the company's history. The Big Fund's involvement is strategically profound: the same state vehicle that invested $95 billion+ across China's semiconductor supply chain (Phases I–III, targeting SMIC, HiSilicon, YMTC, CXMT) is now anchoring China's leading AI model company, creating a direct capital bridge between China's semiconductor self-sufficiency program and its AI model leadership. Phase III Big Fund investment in AI model capability represents an explicit acknowledgment that China's AI sovereignty strategy requires both hardware (chips, fabs) and software (models, frameworks) to be controlled domestically. Tencent and Alibaba — both of which entered separate discussions to invest in DeepSeek — would join as strategic cloud technology partners rather than purely financial investors. Reports indicate Liang Wenfeng is seeking capital primarily to offer employee shareholding to retain researchers being aggressively poached by rival AI labs including ByteDance, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI. DeepSeek has attracted extraordinary talent density with a lean team of approximately 200 core researchers. The $45 billion valuation at first-round pricing compares to Anthropic's $61 billion (March 2025), OpenAI's $300 billion+ (implied by latest rounds), and Mistral AI's $6 billion — placing DeepSeek as the most valuable AI startup in China and among the top five globally. The Big Fund's entry into AI model investment, historically concentrated on semiconductor manufacturing, signals Beijing's formal recognition that AI model capability is now equally strategic to hardware self-sufficiency — the two pillars of Xi Jinping's tech sovereignty doctrine are being unified under the same state investment vehicle.

title: China Mobile Unveils AI-eSIM Product at Mobile Cloud Conference — State Telecom Embeds AI into Telecommunications Infrastructure for IoT, Drones, and Industrial Robots
detail: China Mobile, the world's largest telecommunications operator by subscribers (over 990 million), unveiled its AI-eSIM product at the 2026 Mobile Cloud Conference (held May 7–9 in Suzhou) — embedding artificial intelligence directly into telecommunications infrastructure hardware in a move that extends China's AI deployment ambitions from software models to the physical telecom layer. The AI-eSIM integrates an 'intelligent brain' for dynamic cloud-model dispatching with a hardware-level security chip providing unique device digital identity verification. Initial target applications include AI toys with real-time interactive voice models, smart wearables with health monitoring AI, industrial robotics with edge-AI inference capabilities, and commercial drones requiring secure real-time telemetry. The product's significance extends beyond the specific applications: AI-eSIM enables any physical device with cellular connectivity to access cloud-based AI models on demand, without requiring local AI hardware. China Mobile's state ownership means this infrastructure effectively becomes national AI-physical deployment infrastructure — comparable to 5G base stations as national AI access points. The AI-eSIM launch reflects Beijing's 15th Five-Year Plan strategy of embedding AI into every layer of the national information infrastructure: not just data centers and smartphone applications, but telecommunications chips, IoT sensors, industrial equipment, and consumer devices. China Mobile's distribution network — serving enterprises across manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, and government sectors — gives this product immediate national scale. The technical architecture (cloud-model dispatching via eSIM + hardware security) also addresses a key concern in China's physical AI deployment: device identity and data sovereignty. By routing AI inference through state-controlled cloud infrastructure rather than foreign platforms, the AI-eSIM ensures that physical AI deployment across China remains within domestically auditable information flows — consistent with both China's Data Security Law requirements and its AI governance framework requiring providers to maintain Chinese-user data within Chinese infrastructure.
